note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. Flags: this is a split engine, so the detector is pinned as expected.flaggedIssues via flagsHint "detectFlaggedIssues" with flagsArgs ["state", "result"], mirroring form-app.js's call detectFlaggedIssues(state, grade).

personas.name: low-risk-annual-review
personas.description: Routine annual diabetes review: type 2 diabetes 5 years, both feet sensate with normal pulses, no deformity, callus, or ulceration history — no risk factors on either foot.

note.clinicalContext: No concerns raised at review; patient self-inspects feet weekly.

firedRules.description: Low risk (no risk factors on either foot) — annual review.

personas.name: moderate-risk-single-factor
personas.description: Foot protection clinic follow-up: type 1 diabetes 22 years, right foot has isolated insensate neuropathy (10g monofilament), otherwise clean on both feet — a single risk factor routes to 6-monthly review.

note.clinicalContext: Reduced sensation confirmed on right foot only; annual review upgraded to 6-monthly.

firedRules.description: Moderate risk (one risk factor on the worse foot) — 6-monthly review by the foot protection service.

personas.name: high-risk-combined-factors
personas.description: Type 2 diabetes 15 years, left foot has both insensate neuropathy and diminished pulses plus callus — two combined risk factors with no ulcer/amputation history routes to high risk on the looser 3-monthly interval.

note.clinicalContext: Referred to orthotics for footwear assessment; left foot needs closer monitoring.

firedRules.description: High risk from combined risk factors or renal replacement therapy, without an ulcer/amputation history — 3-monthly review by the multidisciplinary foot team.

flaggedIssues.description: Two or more risk factors combined on at least one foot (e.g. neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease, or either combined with callus/deformity).
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Review referral timing to the multidisciplinary foot team.

flaggedIssues.description: Current footwear is not appropriate for the patient’s risk level.

personas.name: high-risk-previous-ulcer-history
personas.description: Type 2 diabetes 18 years, right foot currently clean on examination but has a documented previous ulcer — history alone forces high risk on the tighter 1-monthly interval regardless of today's findings.

note.clinicalContext: Right foot ulcer healed 8 months ago; admission foot check as part of routine inpatient protocol. Carer assists with foot inspection.

firedRules.description: High risk from previous ulceration/amputation history — 1-monthly review by the multidisciplinary foot team.

personas.name: active-urgent-infected-ulcer
personas.description: Type 1 diabetes 30 years, on renal replacement therapy, left foot has an active infected ulcer — forces active-urgent classification and an urgent multidisciplinary foot team referral regardless of the right foot's findings.

note.clinicalContext: Left foot ulcer discharging and malodorous on admission; urgent multidisciplinary foot team referral made same day.

firedRules.description: An active ulcer or suspected Charcot foot on at least one foot — urgent referral to the multidisciplinary foot team (same or next working day).

flaggedIssues.description: Active ulceration present on at least one foot.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Urgent referral to the multidisciplinary foot team (same or next working day).

flaggedIssues.description: Patient is on renal replacement therapy (dialysis) — an automatic high-risk factor per NICE NG19.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Manage as high risk regardless of current foot examination findings.

flaggedIssues.description: Current footwear is not appropriate for the patient’s risk level.
Patient’s ability to self-inspect and self-care for their feet is impaired, with no support recorded.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange support (carer, family, or service) for regular foot self-inspection.

personas.name: active-urgent-suspected-charcot
personas.description: Type 2 diabetes 12 years, right foot unexplained hot, red, swollen with no clear precipitant — suspected acute Charcot foot forces the same active-urgent, urgent-referral pathway as an active ulcer, even with no ulceration present.

note.clinicalContext: Right foot noted hot and swollen on inspection; same-day referral for suspected Charcot foot, pending imaging.

firedRules.description: An active ulcer or suspected Charcot foot on at least one foot — urgent referral to the multidisciplinary foot team (same or next working day).

flaggedIssues.description: Suspected acute Charcot foot (unexplained hot, red, swollen foot) on at least one foot — a limb-threatening emergency.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Urgent same/next-working-day referral to the multidisciplinary foot team; do not wait for imaging.

flaggedIssues.description: Two or more risk factors combined on at least one foot (e.g. neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease, or either combined with callus/deformity).
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Review referral timing to the multidisciplinary foot team.
